name: Rizhao
title: Rizhao Thickness Measurement | Ore Carriers and Crude Tankers
description: Ship thickness gauging in Rizhao for Capesize ore carriers, VLCCs and bulk carriers: holds, hoppers, ballast tanks, decks and cargo piping measured at berth.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging for Ships at Rizhao's Shijiu and Lanshan Port Areas
intro: Rizhao, on the southern coast of Shandong facing the Yellow Sea, is one of China's leading ports for crude oil and iron ore. VLCCs discharge at the Lanshan jetties for refineries across the province, ore carriers and Capesizes unload for the steel industry, and container and general cargo ships call at the Shijiu area. Most ships are gauged during discharge or while waiting for a berth. Each team flies to the ship from India, with its timing set by the agent's berthing schedule.

highlights.h: Crude tankers at Shandong's pipeline gateway
highlights.p: Rizhao is Sinopec's largest crude landing port and sends crude inland through long-distance pipelines. VLCCs at Lanshan's 300,000-tonne jetties can have deck plating, deck piping and certified ballast tanks gauged while they discharge, under the terminal's permit rules.

Iron ore has long been the port's core dry cargo, much of it for steelworks in Rizhao and across Shandong. Long discharges on Capesizes and larger ore carriers leave holds and ballast tanks free for measurement before the ship sails in ballast.

highlights.h: A pre-docking stop south of Qingdao
highlights.p: Large ships calling at Rizhao normally dock elsewhere, and Qingdao's yards are a short coastal passage north. Readings taken during a Rizhao discharge give the chosen yard a steel estimate before the ship shifts to its dock.

port.h: Rizhao: crude, ore and the southern Shandong coast
p: Rizhao lies on the southern shore of the Shandong Peninsula, between Qingdao to the north-east and Lianyungang to the south, on a stretch of coast with relatively deep water and no river bar to cross. The port has grown in two main areas: Shijiu, the original harbour beside the city, which began as a coal export port and is now a multipurpose port for bulk, containers and general cargo, and Lanshan to the south, developed for crude oil and heavy bulk. Ships approach from the open Yellow Sea, and the anchorages lie offshore of both areas. Winter brings northerly winds and cold-air outbreaks that make launch work uncomfortable, while spring and early summer bring the sea fog that settles over this part of the coast.

Crude oil is the trade that defines Rizhao today. Lanshan has four 300,000-tonne crude jetties, the most recent of which came into operation in October 2023, and Rizhao counts as China's third-largest crude landing port and the largest for Sinopec. From the tank farms, five long-distance pipelines carry crude inland to refineries in Shandong and beyond, which means a steady procession of VLCCs and Suezmaxes arriving laden from long-haul loading ports. Plans for an LNG berth in the Lanshan area have also been approved by national and provincial authorities, with space reserved for a second. For tanker superintendents, the result is a port where large crude carriers spend a predictable time alongside under strict terminal rules, and where the same ship may return several times a year.

Dry bulk is the other pillar. Iron ore once made up the larger part of the port's business and still brings Capesizes and very large ore carriers to dedicated berths, feeding Rizhao's own steelworks and mills further inland, while coal, grain and other bulk cargoes also pass through. Containers have grown at Shijiu on domestic and intra-Asia services. This mix creates two kinds of inspection opportunity: tankers and ore carriers that stay alongside for days while discharging, and smaller bulk carriers and general cargo ships lying idle at anchor while they wait for a berth. Both suit gauging, provided the scope is agreed before the ship arrives and the agent's line-up holds. Where it slips, the plan moves with it rather than forcing work into the wrong spaces.

facilities.h: Where ships are gauged at Rizhao
p: At the Lanshan crude jetties, gauging is limited to what can be done safely on a discharging tanker: deck plating and stiffening, cargo and ballast deck piping, the fire main, and ballast tanks once they are certified gas-free and released by the master. The terminal's hazardous-area rules decide which instruments can be used where, so equipment and procedures are agreed in advance. At the ore and coal berths the work moves into the holds as they are emptied, starting with tank tops and hopper plating, then frames and lower bulkheads, and finishing with ballast tanks as the ship ballasts for departure.

Shijiu's container and general cargo berths give shorter windows, suited to deck structure, hatch coamings and scrubber piping. Ships waiting at the offshore anchorages can be reached by launch when wind and fog allow, which makes them a good place for a buyer's condition survey of a bulk carrier in ballast. Docking is not usually done here; ships move on to the repair yards at Qingdao or elsewhere on the coast, and we pass the Rizhao readings to the yard with each location referenced to the ship's drawings.
list: Lanshan crude jetties — deck, deck piping, fire main and certified ballast tank gauging on VLCCs and Suezmaxes during discharge.
Ore and heavy bulk berths — hold, hopper, frame and inner bottom gauging on Capesizes and very large ore carriers as holds are swept.
Shijiu bulk and general cargo berths — hold, hatch cover and coaming readings on Panamax and Supramax ships.
Shijiu container terminals — deck, coaming and scrubber discharge piping checks during scheduled calls.
Offshore anchorages — pre-docking and pre-purchase gauging on bulk carriers waiting for a berth, weather permitting.

context.h: Port state control, vetting and the Shandong market
p: Rizhao's port state control is run by the China Maritime Safety Administration within the Tokyo MoU framework. With so many large tankers and ore carriers calling, inspectors regularly look at deck and hatch cover condition, ballast tank corrosion, cargo and fire-fighting piping and the structural state of older ships, and deficiencies on those items can mean repairs before the ship is allowed to sail. China's domestic emission control arrangements also apply: open-loop scrubber discharge is restricted in Chinese port waters and some coastal areas, so scrubber-fitted ships often have the system shut down or in closed-loop mode while at Rizhao, and operators should confirm the current rules before arrival.

Commercially, Rizhao sits at the heart of a market built on imported raw materials. Crude buyers in Shandong charter older VLCCs and Suezmaxes as well as modern ones, and charterers and terminals expect documented structural condition from ships in their second decade. Ore carriers on long hauls from Australia and Brazil spend most of their lives laden or in ballast at sea, and a Rizhao discharge may be one of the few occasions when a superintendent can get a team into the holds without booking yard time. Measured readings taken here feed both vetting files and docking plans.

jobs.h: Ship inspection work we see at Rizhao
jobs.p: Jobs at Rizhao follow the two big trades. Tanker managers use the discharge at Lanshan for deck, piping and ballast tank measurements that support vetting or a coming CAP survey; dry bulk superintendents use ore discharges for hold and tank readings before a renewal or intermediate survey; and buyers inspect bulk carriers waiting at anchor. Smaller container and general cargo ships bring narrower scopes such as coamings or scrubber piping. Each programme is checked against the ship's last thickness report and the attending surveyor's expectations, so new readings fall on the same points and corrosion rates can be worked out.
list: Deck, deck longitudinal and ballast tank gauging on a 15-year-old VLCC discharging at Lanshan, ahead of a CAP survey at its next docking.
Fire main and cargo deck piping gauging on a Suezmax with a history of pinhole leaks, done during discharge for vetting.
Hold, hopper and transverse bulkhead gauging on a very large ore carrier after discharge, tracking wastage recorded at the last renewal survey.
Pre-docking steel estimate on a Capesize at a Rizhao ore berth before it shifts to a Qingdao repair yard.
Pre-purchase gauging of a Supramax waiting at the Rizhao anchorage, with hatch covers and topside tanks included for the buyer.

logistics: Rizhao Shanzihe Airport handles domestic flights, and teams usually arrive through Qingdao Jiaodong International Airport and continue by road or rail along the coast. Port passes for the Lanshan crude area, the ore berths and Shijiu are obtained by the ship's agent, and the crude terminal adds its own safety briefing before anyone boards. Technicians travelling from India need Chinese business visas backed by an invitation letter, and some terminals ask for personnel details ahead of arrival, so we begin the application as soon as a likely discharge date is known.

faqs.q: Can cargo tanks be gauged on a VLCC at the Lanshan jetties?
faqs.a: Not while the ship is discharging. Cargo tanks stay closed until they are cleaned, gas-freed and certified, which normally happens in a yard. At the jetty we gauge deck plating and stiffening, deck piping, the fire main and ballast tanks released by the master, all under the terminal's permit rules. That work becomes the first part of a renewal or CAP gauging programme finished in dock.

faqs.q: What is the best time to gauge an ore carrier at Rizhao?
faqs.a: After each hold is discharged and swept, while the ship is still alongside. That gives safe, dry access to the tank top, hopper slopes, lower stools and frames, which carry most of the wear in the ore trade. Ballast tanks follow as the ship ballasts for departure. If the ship waits at anchor before berthing, some ballast tanks can be done then to spread the work.

faqs.q: Is fog a problem for anchorage work off Rizhao?
faqs.a: It can be. In spring and early summer, sea fog over the southern Shandong coast can stop launches and delay pilotage, and in winter strong northerlies do the same. We plan anchorage gauging as weather-dependent and keep priorities clear, so if a transfer is not possible the work moves to the berth stay or to the ship's next port.

faqs.q: Can a job at Rizhao be combined with Qingdao or Lianyungang?
faqs.a: Yes. Qingdao lies up the coast to the north and Lianyungang to the south, and all three ports see the same tankers and ore carriers. If you have ships discharging at more than one of them, or a Rizhao discharge followed by a Qingdao docking, we plan one mobilisation and one visa period to cover them.
